title: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat: create and query Planner tasks and plans
summary: Hold: Microsoft names Planner in Copilot Chat under the Microsoft Copilot licence, contrary to the briefing's statement that its licensing is unpublished. The Planner PowerShell control also needs its documented qualification: it covers Planner Agent chat in premium plans only.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The 23 September 2026 Copilot release notes describe Planner Agent chat inside Planner as a separate item.
claims.quote: Planner integrates Planner Agent chat directly into the app, enabling users to ask questions and manage tasks using natural language.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not describe this feature yet.
claims.quote: Users with a Microsoft Copilot license can use Copilot capabilities in Planner, including Planner Agent, AI-assisted plan creation and task generation, AI-generated status reports, and Planner in Copilot Chat.
claims.fix: Replace the opening two clauses with: 'Microsoft Learn names Planner in Copilot Chat in the Planner service description; the behavioural details below come from the roadmap item and Microsoft's notice.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/microsoft-planner-service-description.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not described which identity this Chat capability uses to call Planner.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner Copilot Chat approval signed in identity license billing; Planner Copilot Chat approval identity. Opened Planner service description, Planner for admins, turn-off-planner-agent and manage-planner-plugin-cowork; only Cowork explicitly identifies its acting identity.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: An approval step before this Chat capability writes a change to Planner is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner capabilities Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat create update plans tasks licensing meter approval identity admin disable; Planner Copilot Chat approval identity. Opened Planner service description and manage-planner-plugin-cowork; the documented approval rule is for Cowork.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Planner Plugin can be blocked in Microsoft 365 admin center under Agents > Tools > Planner Plugin > Users > Block.
claims.quote: To block the plugin, go to Agents > Tools, select Planner Plugin, open the Users tab, and select Block.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block is the package-block operation for the plugin availability control.
claims.quote:
Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block
claims.fix: Keep the call and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/package/overview as the additional source establishing that a package represents an agent or a tool such as a plugin. Replace the caution about the plugin not being called a package with: 'The Package Management API manages agents and tools, including plugins, in the organisation catalog.' Keep the separate caveat about this Chat capability.

claims.claim: The Planner Plugin management page names Global Administrator or Copilot Administrator as the required admin role.
claims.quote: Admin role | Global Administrator or Copilot Administrator

claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: Blocking the Planner Plugin affects new conversations while conversations already in progress continue until they end.
claims.quote: Blocking applies to new conversations. Conversations already in progress continue until they end.

claims.claim: In the documented Cowork experience, every Planner change is shown to the user and requires approval.
claims.quote: Every change to Planner is shown to the user and requires their approval.

claims.claim: Set-PlannerConfiguration -AllowPlannerCopilot $true -PlannerCopilotAllowedGroupId <security group id> enables the documented Planner experiences for a security group.
claims.quote:
To turn on Planner Agent and Planner Agent chat for a specific security group:
Set-PlannerConfiguration -AllowPlannerCopilot $true -PlannerCopilotAllowedGroupId <security group id>

claims.claim: An admin UI equivalent for the AllowPlannerCopilot and PlannerCopilotAllowedGroupId control is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: AllowPlannerCopilot PlannerCopilotAllowedGroupId admin center UI setting. Opened turn-off-planner-agent and manage-copilot-agents-integrated-apps; the former documents PowerShell, while the latter manages agents without documenting a UI for these Planner settings.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; controls[1].note; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The Planner configuration control covers Planner Agent and Planner Agent chat in Planner without a plan-type qualification.
claims.quote: restrict access to the Planner Agent experience for task execution and status reporting in both basic and premium plans as well as the Planner Agent chat in premium plans only.
claims.fix: Change controls[1].governs and its rendered label to 'Who can use Planner Agent (basic and premium plans) and Planner Agent chat (premium plans only), all users or one security group'. Add 'The documented chat restriction covers premium plans only' to its note, and retain that qualification in prose describing the control's coverage. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/planner/turn-off-planner-agent.

claims.claim: Get-PlannerConfiguration reads the current Planner configuration settings.
claims.quote:
To verify your settings, run the following command:
Get-PlannerConfiguration

claims.claim: Changes to the documented Planner configuration policy can take up to one hour.
claims.quote: Changes may take up to 1 hour to reflect across your organization.

claims.claim: Setting AllowPlannerCopilot to false is a documented way to turn off the Planner experiences covered by that policy.
claims.quote:
To turn off Planner Agent and Planner Agent chat for all users:
Set-PlannerConfiguration -AllowPlannerCopilot $false

claims.claim: The package block operation's reference page does not specifically name the Planner Plugin as a Copilot package.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner Plugin copilot/admin/catalog/packages. Opened copilotpackage-block and the Package Management API overview. The block reference does not name Planner Plugin; the overview establishes the broader class of plugins as packages.

claims.claim: The capability's licensing model is included within the licence that entitles users to the relevant Copilot functionality.
claims.quote: Users with a Microsoft Copilot license can use Copilot capabilities in Planner, including Planner Agent, AI-assisted plan creation and task generation, AI-generated status reports, and Planner in Copilot Chat.
claims.fix: Keep licensing.model as 'included', but identify the covering licence in its notes: 'The Planner service description lists Planner in Copilot Chat among the capabilities available to users with a Microsoft Copilot licence. A meter specific to this capability is not yet published.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/microsoft-planner-service-description rather than relying solely on the base Copilot Chat requirement.

claims.claim: The notice names no separate data boundary for this feature.
claims.quote:
Existing Planner permissions and access controls continue to apply.

No changes to existing Planner data storage or permissions are expected.
